title: Oath and Crown
premise: Kestrel Oyelaran, a debt-bound scribe in the Ledgerhouse of Saint Veyra, has spent her life recording the guild's trades in impossible things—bottled grief, borrowed years, names sold at auction. When prayers to the old gods begin receiving answers no one sent, Kestrel traces the miracle-trade back to its source: a crown that eats kings and speaks with their voices. To unbind King Aldric from the thing wearing him, she must gather the scattered found family of her own hidden past—including the mother who sold her name to pay her debts—and offer up the one memory she swore never to trade: her own. In the end, Kestrel breaks her ledger-line by giving the memory freely, unbinding the king but losing herself, until her found family writes her back into the world, name first.
about_author: J. M. Joubert is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate ledgers in coastal trading towns before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about paperwork, inheritance, and the quiet violence of being remembered wrong.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. We meet her balancing the Ledgerhouse's impossible accounts, invisible among the guild's traders, when a prayer-scroll arrives bearing an answer written in a dead god's hand. The emotional beat is wary longing: Kestrel recognizes the handwriting as her mother's, though her mother has been dead-ledgered for years.

chapters.title: What the Guild Buys
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She investigates the prayer-trade through the guild's back rooms, discovering bottled miracles moving through official channels toward the palace. Her supervisor, Master Corvane, warns her off with unusual gentleness. The beat is dread mixed with the first thrill of agency—she chooses to keep digging.

chapters.title: A King Who Answers Twice
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Kestrel and King Aldric. Summoned to audit palace accounts, Kestrel witnesses the king answer the same petition twice, once kindly and once cruelly, in two different voices. Aldric's POV reveals he knows something wears his crown. The beat is horror laced with unexpected kinship.

chapters.title: The Name on the Old Page
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Following ledger-threads into the archive of burned records, she finds her own childhood entry: her name was collateral for her mother's debt, sold to the Ledgerhouse itself. The beat is betrayal curdling into resolve; her invisibility was purchased, not chosen.

chapters.title: Thieves, Saints, and Other Family
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV chapter. Kestrel tracks down the people tied to her old page: Sefa, a debt-thief who knew her as a child; Brother Ilem, a defrocked priest who still prays; and her mother, alive, working the guild's lowest floor. The beat is fragile, awkward hope—the found family assembling itself.

chapters.title: The Crown Remembers
chapters.summary: Aldric's POV. The entity in the crown, called the Regent, begins overwriting Aldric's memories with its own ancient reign, and it notices Kestrel's investigation. It sends her a gift: a perfect restoration of one of her stolen memories. The beat is seduction—being seen fully, at last, at a terrible price.

chapters.title: Terms of Surrender
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The Regent offers a contract: her remaining memories in exchange for her mother's freedom and the guild's dissolution. Master Corvane is revealed as the Regent's original broker, bound like her. The beat is despair and clarity; Kestrel understands the only way out is a trade the Regent cannot price.

chapters.title: Everything Owed
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. The family raids the Ledgerhouse vaults to steal back every name held as collateral, including Kestrel's. Sefa is gravely wounded holding the door; Ilem burns his last holy relic to blind the Regent's sight-lines. The beat is sacrifice freely given—the opposite of everything the guild trades in.

chapters.title: The Unbinding
chapters.summary: Climax, Kestrel's POV. In the throne room, Kestrel offers the Regent not a sale but a gift: her final memory, given without terms, which no contract can hold. The gift unravels the logic of the crown; Aldric breaks free as the Regent starves on an unpayable kindness. The beat is terrible, luminous self-loss.

chapters.title: Written Back
chapters.summary: Resolution, ensemble POV. Kestrel wakes blank-named in the ruined Ledgerhouse, and her family does what the guild never could: they write her back, each contributing a true memory of her into a new kind of ledger. Aldric reforms the guild into a house of returns. The beat is quiet joy—inheritance remade as something shared rather than owed.
